messages.author: 2f5df0366d20510f
messages.subject: QTL analysis with quantitative covariate
parts:
Dear Prof. Karl,

Now, I want to add a quantitative covariate (proline content) to my qtl analysis. Anova and boxplot show that it is a additive covariate, as expected. But, I do not know what is wrong in my command entering that after adding the covariate, my main qtl (LOD:22.3) declined, and now it is not significant.
Would you please clarify it for me? Thank you very much.
Regards,
Farah,

If the covariate is highly correlated with the primary phenotype, you may be eliminating the QTL effect by conditioning on it.
That is, if the effects are Q -> X -> Y, where Q is the QTL, X is the covariate, and Y is the phenotype, then you'll eliminate the QTL effect by conditioning on X.

See chapter 7 of the R/qtl book (http://www.rqtl.org/book).


Ok. Thanks Prof. In this case, I can not add effect of covariate in the qtl analysis?

Best,
Farah,

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL analysis with quantitative covariate
parts:
Whether or not to include the covariate depends on your goals, but you do need to be careful about the meaning of the results, when you include a secondary phenotype as a covariate.

karl

parts:
Dear Prof. Karl,

Thank you very much. But, when Pearson’s correlation between my phenotype and covariate (proline) is 0.61 at the 0.01 level, how I can find whether my covariate is additive or interactive?
I did Anova:

Analysis of Variance Table

              Df     Sum Sq       Mean Sq      F value           Pr(>F)   

proline     1     265973         265973        109.78           < 2.2e-16 ***

Residuals 187 453078    2423 

 

***************************************************************************

I also did makeqtl & fitqtl in this way (out<- scanone(alico2, addcovar=covar,method="hk") :


Drop one QTL at a time ANOVA table:

---------------------------------- 

                df       Type III SS         LOD            %var           F value            Pvalue(Chi2)          Pvalue(F)   

4...@34.5     2       42733               4.864            5.682          11.58                  0                      1.84e-05 ***

8...@68.2     2      259983             23.330           34.571          70.43                 0                      < 2e-16 ***


**************************************************************************


Estimated effects:

-----------------

                  est         SE            t

Intercept    65.131     3.148      20.689

4...@34.5a   24.935     5.226      4.771

4...@34.5d   -5.367      6.530     -0.822

8...@68.2a    54.129    4.616     11.726

8...@68.2d   -13.488    6.405     -2.106



Would you please clarify me that based on my results my covariate is additive or interactive?

Thank you so much, in advance.


Best Regards,

Farah

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL analysis with quantitative covariate
parts:
The question is then whether there is a QTL x covariate interaction, which you could investigate by fitting the model with the covariate as strictly additive and then as interactive, and taking the difference in LOD scores; if large, that indicates that there is evidence for a QTL x covariate interaction.

I would also look at a scatterplot of the phenotype and the covariate, with points colored by there QTL genotype.

karl
